description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Jerome Gambit. Meet 4.Bxf7+ with the calm king walk and refute the sacrifice.

drills.briefExplanation: 3...Bc5 4.Bxf7+ Kxf7 5.Nxe5+ Ke6! — take the bishop, then walk the king; never grab the knight.
drills.description: Black to play. White is hinting at the Jerome — develop 3...Bc5 and be ready for 4.Bxf7+.
drills.explanation: Against the Jerome, Black's rule is simple: take the bishop, then move the KING, not the knight. After 4.Bxf7+ Kxf7 5.Nxe5+ the greedy 5...Nxe5?? loses on the spot; the refutation is 5...Ke6! — the king strolls through the center (6.Qg4+ Kf7) and reaches safety on e8. White sacrificed a bishop for nothing, and Black's extra piece decides.
drills.name: The Calm King Walk

drills.briefExplanation: 5...Ke6 6.Qg4+ Kf6 — keep walking; the checks run out and the extra bishop remains.
drills.description: Black to play. The sacrifice is on the board and White checks on e5 — find the only correct king move.
drills.explanation: The critical moment of the whole gambit. 5...Ke6! is the only move — 5...Nxe5?? and 5...Ke8?? both lose. After 6.Qg4+ Kf6! the king keeps walking toward the kingside, where White has no more checks: the queen checks are exhausted, the knights can't reach, and Black consolidates a bishop up. Precision under fire is the defender's art.
drills.name: Walking Through Checks

name: Jerome Gambit — Black Tactics
